gaps.sentence: Such ___ the chaos at the airport that hundreds slept on the terminal floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Such was the chaos that…' — emphatic fronting of 'such' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Seldom have I been so ___ by a performance.
gaps.explanation: 'moved' — the audience was emotionally affected; inversion with have been.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ a debut film attracted such wide attention.
gaps.explanation: 'Rarely has a debut film attracted …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
gaps.explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.

gaps.sentence: Only after the interview ___ I realise how nervous I had been.
gaps.explanation: Only after X did I realise… — inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: Only after the audit ___ the missing funds come to light.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after the audit did the funds come to light'.
